characterization_methods.key_findings: Steel is negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate sensitive; flow stress increases with ε̇ and decreases with T; reproducibility of the experiments was checked on the same steel batch.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 900–1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1; 60% compression (true strain 0.92); cylindrical φ8 mm × 12 mm specimens; this sample at 900 °C/10 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire flow stress curves to analyse hot deformation behavior, determine DRX activation energy/Z parameter and build the DRX state diagram
characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression (flow-curve / rheological stress measurement)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant = 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.key_findings: DRX degree: large deformation zone (3) > small deformation zone (2) > difficult deformation zone (1); DRX fraction and grain size increase with T and decrease with ε̇.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed samples split in half along the axial axis, prepared, ground, polished and etched; 100 µm scale bars on micrographs
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe initial microstructure and microstructure evolution in the three deformation zones after hot compression
characterization_methods.technique: optical metallography (laser confocal microscopy) of etched sections

analytical_models.equation_role: temperature-compensated strain-rate parameter characterising the combined effect of T and ε̇
analytical_models.model_note: Table 1 gives lnZ for all T and ε̇; for the 10 s^-1 row and 900 °C column lnZ = 70.99, the highest value in the matrix.

analytical_models.equation_role: multiple-linear-regression models relating critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress to lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Alloy-level regression (R ranged 0.911–0.957); εc/εp ≈ 0.452 determined via the Cingara-McQueen equation and Poliak-Jonas inflection criterion.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Applied to the full experimental matrix (900–1150 °C; ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1); for this sample at T = 900 °C, ε̇ = 10 s^-1
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine Eq. (1); Qp = 669.844 kJ mol^-1; material constants α = 0.00599, k1 = 5.135, k2 = 15.690; Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT)
computational_details.simulation_method: analytical constitutive analysis (Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine + Zener-Hollomon parameter)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Z increases with ε̇ and decreases with T, matching the trend of the flow stress; the text notes the experimental phenomena have reproducibility.

analytical_models.equation_role: predict DRX average grain size from strain rate, temperature (and initial grain size/strain)
analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 11/12)
analytical_models.model_note: Initial grain size and strain were taken as fixed constants, so a·d0^h·ε^p collapses into a single coefficient.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: FF simulation set-up: billet as rigid-plastic body, die as rigid body, semi-symmetric specimen model, contact friction set to shear type with value 0.3, billet-air convection coefficient 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation conditions matched the thermal-compression experiment.
computational_details.simulation_method: mathematical regression of experimental DRX grain size (for numerical simulation)
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D finite element software (target application); Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation algorithm for regression
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted vs experimental DRX grain size: correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%; absolute error mostly within 3 µm.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooled from the 1200 °C homogenisation hold to the 900 °C deformation temperature.

Strain rate for this sample is 10 s^-1 (highest of the 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 s^-1 set); mica foils with high-temperature lubricants applied on both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity; carried out on a Gleeble-3500 simulator.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to 60% (maximum true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on both end faces; Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; water-spray cooling after deformation.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Grains large relative to the 100 µm scale bar; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length (no numeric value given).

microstructure_list.region: bulk of the forging billet (pre-deformation reference state)

structures.overall_structure: Pre-deformation (as-forged billet) microstructure: large polygonal grains delimited by a bright, continuous, slightly etched boundary network, enclosing dark grey grain interiors that carry many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations/lamellae whose direction changes from grain to grain, i.e. strongly banded dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution.

grain_structure.average_grain_size: approximately 8 µm (lowest of the four strain-rate series at 900 °C)

microstructure_list.region: core of the compressed specimen = large deformation zone (zone 3)

structures.overall_structure: Hot-deformed (DRX) microstructure after 60% compression at 900 °C/10 s^-1: dynamic recrystallization occurs but is insufficient at low T and high ε̇ — small DRX grains together with large remnant original (elongated) grains remain, giving poor microstructural homogeneity. (No dedicated 900 °C micrograph is shown; behaviour follows from the low-T(900–950 °C)/high-ε̇(1–10 s^-1) description and the 950 °C/1 s^-1 panel.)

unmapped_findings: For the 900 °C/10 s^-1 condition the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 70.99 (Table 1, 10 s^-1 row, 900 °C column) — the highest value in the tested 6-temperature × 4-strain-rate matrix, indicating the most severe hot-deformation condition (b0037, table_001).

The peak stress at 900 °C/10 s^-1 is not stated numerically in the text: the Fig. 3(d) colour-bar upper bound of 486.0 MPa corresponds to the lowest-temperature/highest-strain-rate corner (900 °C, 10 s^-1), while the text only quantifies peak stress at 0.01 s^-1 (305.4 MPa at 900 °C falling to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, an 82% reduction) and states a 73% reduction between 900 and 1150 °C at 10 s^-1; therefore the 486 MPa value is inferred from the colour-bar maximum rather than explicitly attributed (b0024, figure_003).

For the low-temperature/high-strain-rate regime (900–950 °C at 1–10 s^-1) the DRX grains are small but the dynamic recrystallization is insufficient — large original grains remain and the microstructure homogeneity is poor; the DRX average grain size at 900 °C lies between roughly 8 and 13 µm for the four strain rates, being smallest for 10 s^-1 (b0063, b0065, figure_010, figure_011).
This 900 °C/10 s^-1 condition lies outside the processing window recommended for fine and uniform grains (950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1) (b0012, b0065, b0086).

No microstructure micrograph is shown specifically at 900 °C; the 900 °C microstructure is described only through the general low-T/high-ε̇ text and the analogous 950 °C/1 s^-1 panel (Fig. 9(d)) (b0061, b0063, figure_009).
